title: Guide exercise: semi-stable extensions, blocking
description: A starter on a fresh problem: the loop of the library example af-semi-stable with every refinement replaced by a block. Find the interface, write a refinement, and compare with af-semi-stable. See the guide page "Loop shapes".

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% An argumentation framework without a stable extension (z attacks itself).
arg(a;b;c;d;e;f;g;h;i;j;z).
att(a,b). att(b,a).                 % a and b attack each other
att(i,j). att(j,i).                 % so do i and j
att(b,j). att(j,b).                 % and b and j
att(b,c). att(c,d). att(d,e). att(e,c).     % b attacks the cycle c, d, e
att(j,f). att(f,g). att(g,h). att(h,f).     % j attacks the cycle f, g, h
att(z,z).
fragments.description: The framework. Added to every solver.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% A candidate: an admissible set, that is, a set that is conflict-free and attacks
% all its attackers.
{ in(A) } :- arg(A).
:- in(A), in(B), att(A,B).
beaten(A) :- in(B), att(B,A).
:- in(A), att(B,A), not beaten(B).
% Its range: the members and the arguments they attack.
range(A) :- in(A).
range(A) :- beaten(A).
#show in/1.
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): admissible sets, and their range.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
% The check compares ranges only.
glue(range(A)) :- arg(A).
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the range of the set (derived atoms), not its members.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: an admissible set whose range contains the candidate's range and
% one more argument.
{ big(A) } :- arg(A).
:- big(A), big(B), att(A,B).
hit(A) :- big(B), att(B,A).
:- big(A), att(B,A), not hit(B).
wide(A) :- big(A).
wide(A) :- hit(A).
:- range(A), not wide(A).
gain(A) :- wide(A), not range(A).
wider :- gain(A).
:- not wider.
#show big/1.

% The counterexample refutes every set whose range stays inside its range and misses
% one argument of it. So: an argument outside the wider range enters the candidate's
% range, or the first gained argument does.
relevant(range(A)) :- arg(A), not wide(A).
relevant(range(A)) :- gain(A), not gain(B) : arg(B), B < A.
fragments.description: Looks for an admissible set with a larger range (solver C).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)
